name: Retinal Degeneration-Nanophthalmos-Glaucoma Syndrome
aliases: Nanophthalmos with Retinal Degeneration and Glaucoma

criteria.description: Presence of nanophthalmos characterized by abnormally small eyes with short axial length
Evidence of progressive retinal degeneration including pigmentary changes and photoreceptor loss
Clinical diagnosis of glaucoma with elevated intraocular pressure and optic nerve damage
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance
Ocular imaging showing reduced axial length and retinal structural abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: nanophthalmos, retinal degeneration, and glaucoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory

imaging: Ultrasound biomicroscopy showing reduced axial length and thickened sclera
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) revealing retinal thinning and photoreceptor loss
Gonioscopy demonstrating narrow or closed anterior chamber angles
genetic: Mutations in MFRP gene associated with nanophthalmos and retinal degeneration
Possible autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance patterns
other: Elevated intraocular pressure measurements via tonometry

distinguishingFeatures: Nanophthalmos without associated retinal degeneration or glaucoma
Absence of progressive retinal pigmentary changes
Retinal degeneration without nanophthalmos or elevated intraocular pressure

redFlags: Sudden onset of painful red eye indicating acute glaucoma attack
Signs of retinal detachment such as flashes and floaters
references: MFRP gene mutations in nanophthalmos and retinal degeneration: A review, J Med Genet, 2018
Clinical features and management of nanophthalmos and associated glaucoma, Ophthalmology, 2020
